g.text: StatBus Upgrade Timeline (single service; observed-state decides direction — already-at-new continues forward, cannot-reach-new rolls back)
The only way to know these paths actually work is to RUN them — the problem is too hard
to reason out. commit -> push -> CI builds the per-commit image -> run on a real VM ->
observe -> iterate. This diagram is the map (each case + its TEST coverage); the run is
the territory. See doc/install-upgrade-testing.md.

Fresh install — seed restore (first boot, before any upgrade)
./sb install (StateFresh) — Seed step:
./sb db seed fetch (pull statbus-seed:<commit_short>) + pg_restore --single-transaction
./sb migrate up — apply only the migrations newer than the seed
Fresh DB only: checkSeedRestored gates the Seed step OFF when the DB holds
user data or applied migrations — a seed restore never overwrites a populated DB.
Seed CREATION is a CI/dev activity — see DEVELOPMENT.md § Database seed.
Service boot
start statbus-upgrade@$USER.service (Type=notify, Restart=always)
advisory lock + LISTEN upgrade channel
(cheap, bounded init)
sd_notify READY=1
(emitted here — heavy recovery below runs in the ACTIVE phase under WatchdogSec)
boot migrate up — schema to the daemon FLOOR (schema-skew guard; STATBUS-145 --to floor)
recoverFromFlag — reconcile a flag left on disk (flag-DRIVEN)
completeInProgressUpgrade — reconcile an in_progress row with NO flag
(flag-INDEPENDENT belt; the SOLE recovery for a pre-flight kill)
Two-layer boot recovery. recoverFromFlag handles a kill AFTER the flag exists (Phase
ladder: old-sb-upgrading / new-sb-swapped / new-sb-upgrading /
rollback-schema-floor-failed / rollback_finishing). The floor-failed arm is
daemon alive-idle; rollback_finishing is cleanup-only before observed state.
completeInProgressUpgrade handles a kill BEFORE
the flag exists — the claim -> writeUpgradeFlag window (see § old-sb-upgrading).
It rolls such an orphan to a named terminal state via verifyUpgradeGroundTruth.
TEST COVERAGE — boot
TEST 1-boot-startup-timeout: startup past TimeoutStartSec stays bounded —
heavy work runs post-READY=1 under WatchdogSec, never the static start budget.
TEST 1-boot-advisory-too-early: an advisory-lock attempt before the DB is ready
exits 42 and systemd restarts cleanly — no start-loop wedge.
TEST flagless-selfheal-at-target-arc: the belt converges a REAL flagless AT-TARGET
orphan row (real dispatch, real flag truncation) to completed on the next ordinary
boot ([completed-from-in-progress], serve-proven).
TEST boot-migrate-churn-alive-idle-arc: a FLAGLESS boot-migrate that fails
deterministically (exit 20) banners ONCE and stays alive-idle — never the
restart-loop into StartLimit death (STATBUS-144).
NO TEST (gap): the belt's BEHIND half — a flagless orphan from a pre-flight kill
(the claim -> writeUpgradeFlag window) rolled to a named terminal — is unproven;
its rollback leg currently inherits the PREVIOUS upgrade's pre-upgrade pin
(STATBUS-197, ruled; fix design pending). See the preflight-kill gap under
§ old-sb-upgrading.
Schedule + dispatch
./sb upgrade apply-latest →
UPDATE state='scheduled' + NOTIFY
Deploy contract (STATBUS-040/-041): deploy scripts
(standalone.sh / cloud.sh) NEVER pre-stop the service —
systemctl stop is SIGTERM, which an in-flight upgrade
answers with a rollback. ./sb install itself refuses a
progressing upgrade and takes over a crash-looping one
(SIGKILL-class). Binary swaps are atomic renames — no
stop needed for those either.
NOTIFY wakes the listener
claim row WHERE state='scheduled' → in_progress
(started_at set, error=NULL — NO flag on disk yet)
+ reset-failed on own unit (NRestarts counts THIS upgrade only — STATBUS-039 F2)
TEST COVERAGE — schedule + dispatch
TEST claim-without-notify-arc: the daemon claims a pending scheduled row WITHOUT a live
NOTIFY (startup-scan / heartbeat tick) — a NOTIFY lost while the daemon is down never
strands a row (STATBUS-098).
TEST deploy-status-proof-arc: the deploy pipeline's RED path — a broken release rolls
back autonomously and the CI-side status poll reports the TRUE terminal, never a
false green (STATBUS-170).
old-sb-upgrading — backup + binary swap
pre-flight — NO flag on disk yet (row is in_progress, error=NULL)
pre-flight checks — downgrade guard, release assets, disk, signature
Flag-absent window — spans the claim above through pre-flight, until writeUpgradeFlag.
A kill HERE leaves the row in_progress | error=NULL with NO flag: recoverFromFlag finds
nothing to reconcile, so completeInProgressUpgrade (§ Service boot) is the ONLY recovery
— it rolls the row back with a named reason at the next boot.
NO TEST (gap): preflight-kill — a kill in the claim -> writeUpgradeFlag window must converge
the row to a named terminal state via the belt at next boot. STATBUS-197 (ruled): the
belt's rollback leg currently inherits the PREVIOUS upgrade's pre-upgrade pin here
(backup_path empty — nothing was ever touched); fix design pending. Candidate inject:
a claim-window KillHere class (an ADDITION to the inject vocabulary).
mutex held — Holder="service", flock LOCK_EX on the upgrade-in-progress marker

Fail-fast: any step, before or after the swap, that errors OR hangs aborts the
single attempt and routes to rollback (§ Complete / rollback). No retry.
TEST COVERAGE — old-sb-upgrading (mutex held; real-dispatch arcs)
TEST preswap-backup-kill-arc: a kill during the DB snapshot converges the row to a named
terminal — rolled_back, or failed if the restore also fails — never stranded in_progress;
a partial pre-upgrade-SYNCING dir is never promoted to active.
TEST preswap-checkout-kill-arc: a kill during git checkout converges to terminal; the
unswapped binary keeps serving the old version.
TEST preswap-binary-swap-kill-arc: a kill at the replaceBinaryOnDisk pivot is recovered (new-sb-swapped
resume or rollback) — never a half-swapped row that lies about the running version.
new-sb-swapped → new-sb-upgrading — continuing after a crash-restart
exit 42 —
old-sb-swap
: switch to the new sb, request the ONE planned respawn
restart unit on the new binary
fresh boot: cheap init -> READY=1 (watchdog arms)
boot-migrate-up — schema up to the DAEMON FLOOR only (migrate up --to DaemonSchemaFloor)
The new binary BOOTS FRESH — nothing continues in memory; it re-runs the full Service-boot
sequence: cheap init -> READY=1 -> boot-migrate-up -> recoverFromFlag.
STATBUS-145: boot-migrate catches the schema up ONLY to the daemon's operating floor, NOT to
HEAD. The upgrade DELTA is above the floor and runs EXACTLY ONCE at the applyPostSwap migrate
step below — that step is now the real, killable delta site, NOT a no-op. So a death mid-delta
leaves the schema positively Behind → data-safe rollback (the atomicity flip), and boot-migrate
runs only the small, rare FLOOR migrations. boot-migrate runs post-READY with the watchdog armed
and no other WATCHDOG=1 source alive, so it carries its OWN always-ping ticker, bounded by the
shared MigrateUpTimeout (12 h ceiling, STATBUS-095; same exemption as the applyPostSwap migrate).
recoverFromFlag (service.go:682) then READS the upgrade-in-progress marker's phase to learn where the
prior process died. Phase progresses old-sb-upgrading "" (:197) -> new-sb-swapped "post_swap" (stamped
:403, before exit 42) -> new-sb-upgrading (stamped :4339, as resume commits; stored: "resuming").
The SAME dispatch runs on EVERY boot — the planned exit-42 here, or any unplanned-death restart.

recoverFromFlag is a phase dispatch: the marker phase decides direction BEFORE anything destructive.
new-sb-swapped (post_swap) → continue forward; old-sb-upgrading ("") → roll back (nothing changed);
corrupt/unreadable marker → discard-and-log, normal start; unrecognized phase → [HUMAN: unknown].
new-sb-upgrading (resuming) → observed-state decides: already-at-new → complete forward;
cannot-reach-new → identity-keyed roll back; can't-read-position (db-unreachable or commit-not-fetched)
→ error classifier (see lifecycle diagram §3): intermittent → backoff-retry, exhausts → roll back.
Full decision tree: see upgrade-lifecycle diagram · doc/upgrade-recovery-model.md.
STATBUS-046 — crash-resume ATTEMPT BUDGET (the per-class routing at the failure chokepoint):
every resumePostSwap entry is one forward ATTEMPT — recovery_attempts++ at attempt START, so a
death self-counts. resumeEscalation bounds the loop that gave rune 10,229 restarts:
• budget = 3 PROCESS DEATHS (deaths = attempts−1) exhausted, OR same-step-twice (deterministic hang, from the flag's dying-step) → TERMINAL
• already-at-new (can't roll back — integrators wrote past maintenance-off) → PARK:
recovery_parked_at + reason; row stays in_progress; service skips resume (alive-idle); siren ONCE
• data-safe / cannot-reach-new → roll back (039 owns direction; 110 makes it byte-safe)
Class A (readiness) waits IN PLACE (size-scaled) and NEVER consumes an attempt; B (deterministic) +
C (resource) → park on first. Un-park = the two deliberate operator triggers only, each a
single fresh attempt with a reset budget.
INVARIANT — a death in the delta window (the STATBUS-145 atomicity flip; re-derive from
the cells below): a death BEFORE the delta starts re-applies forward on restart (nothing
recorded, nothing lost) -> completed. A death MID-delta — ledger advanced, or a
committed-but-unrecorded object — reads observed Behind -> one-shot data-safe rollback.
The delta applies exactly once or restores; never a blind forward re-run of a
half-applied delta.
TEST COVERAGE — phase dispatch + resume after the swap (real-dispatch arcs, STATBUS-071)
THE PARK SUBSTRATE (STATBUS-046, proven on the real path):
TEST postswap-health-park-arc: a POST-delta at-target health failure PARKS the row —
recovery_parked_at + named reason, siren exactly ONCE per park event, alive-idle,
parked-skip on every automatic resume; a deliberate un-park grants ONE fresh attempt;
a genuine fix release DISPLACES the standing park (superseded, story intact — STATBUS-159).
TEST un-park-to-completion-arc: a RESOURCE-class park, both arms — a DELTA upgrade +
resource failure rolls back and re-triggers; a NO-DELTA upgrade parks AT-TARGET on the
named shortfall, the operator frees it, ./sb install grants exactly ONE fresh attempt,
the SAME row completes with ZERO restores.
LOGIC-PIN (no on-cue real-path construction under the STATBUS-145 geometry): the D-class
same-step-twice and budget-exhaust park decisions are pinned by
cli/internal/upgrade/recovery_escalation_test.go.
THE COMMIT<->RECORD CELLS — all fire at the applyPostSwap migrate step (the ONE delta
site, STATBUS-145), never at the floor-bounded boot-migrate. THE RULED RULE
(STATBUS-071 map, three proving runs): a migrate-window death BEFORE the delta starts
-> forward, the delta applies fresh -> completed. A death MID-delta with the ledger
already advanced -> observed Behind -> one-shot rollback -> rolled_back.
In execution order:
(1) TEST postswap-mid-migration-kill-arc: parent-kill before the delta's first tx
opens -> forward re-applies cleanly -> completed.
(2) TEST postswap-mid-tx-kill-arc: kill INSIDE an uncommitted pre-delta tx — Postgres
aborts it (no committed-but-unrecorded state) -> forward -> completed. The green
control proving the boundary's SAFE side.
(3) TEST postswap-after-commit-kill-arc (the daemon PARENT killed) +
after-commit-before-recorded-kill-arc (the migrate SUBPROCESS killed): the ~ms
window AFTER a migration commits, BEFORE its ledger INSERT — forward re-apply
would lie ("relation already exists") -> RESTORE -> rolled_back (the lost-stamp
shape; STATBUS-013/105, the King's ratified rule).
(4) TEST postswap-between-migrations-kill-arc: kill AFTER V1 records, BEFORE V2 opens
(MID-delta, ledger advanced) -> observed Behind on the first read -> one-shot
rollback -> rolled_back.
(e) TEST failing-arc: a migration that errors EVERY apply -> rolled_back with the DB
logically identical to the pre-upgrade baseline -> the FIXED release applies fresh.
THE DELTA UNDER DURESS:
TEST postswap-migration-timeout-arc: a >WatchdogSec-slow delta migration is NOT
watchdog-killed — the always-ping ticker covers it (STATBUS-012); slow-but-live survives.
TEST postswap-migration-ceiling-arc: a delta past the hard MigrateUpTimeout ceiling is
killed by OUR OWN bound -> rolled back, orphan backend reaped, clean slate.
TEST postswap-migration-oom-arc: the OS OOM-kills Postgres mid-delta -> observed Behind
-> one-shot restore -> rolled_back, clean-slate fingerprint equals baseline.
THE RESUME TAIL:
TEST postswap-container-restart-kill-arc: a kill between app-services start and the
health check converges — the resume re-runs the steps idempotently.
TEST postswap-watchdog-reconnect-arc: a slow-but-advancing DB reconnect is kept alive by
the deferGating WATCHDOG=1 ticker; a true hang is reaped by connect()'s own ctx, not
the watchdog.
TEST postswap-converged-selfheal-arc: a crash in the ~ms window AFTER convergence (delta
applied, serving, maintenance off) but BEFORE the completed write lands -> the next
boot self-heals the row to completed ([completed-self-heal], serve-proven —
STATBUS-192; the parked-guard skip holds — STATBUS-193).
TEST cross-version-rename-handoff-arc: a box installed at a PRE-RENAME release hands its
mid-upgrade flag across the swap; the new binary's legacy-alias phase read routes it
correctly (STATBUS-164).
DEFERRED (still a scenario, ASSESS): 3-postswap-worker-ddl-deadlock — a worker-locked
migration stays bounded via pre-DDL quiesce; intent, not proven coverage.
INVARIANT — lost-stamp window (re-derive from cells (3)/(e) above):
The migration done-stamp is written in a SEPARATE transaction from the migration DDL -> that gap
is the lost-stamp window. A kill in that gap leaves a committed-but-unrecorded schema object;
forward re-apply fails ("relation already exists") -> cannot-reach-new -> one-shot rollback.
Complete / rollback

TEST COVERAGE — complete / rollback (real-dispatch arcs)
TEST rollback-kill-arc: a kill mid-rollback() still converges to a terminal state
on the next recovery pass.
TEST postswap-rollback-restore-watchdog-arc: a STALLED DB restore keeps the box alive via
the heartbeat (NRestarts frozen through the stall) -> rolled_back, byte-identical clean slate.
TEST rollback-pair-terminal-arc: TWO consecutive rollback process-deaths -> the restore-broke
terminal (state=failed, human summoned) at EXACTLY 2 — never a third attempt (STATBUS-134).
TEST restore-broke-reattempt-arc: the STATBUS-111 human-gated replay — ./sb install on a
failed row with a retained snapshot completes the restore to an honest rolled_back; a
STILL-CORRUPT git tree REFUSES actionably before any destructive step — never a mixed-era box.
TEST transient-db-backoff-arc: a TRANSIENT DB outage mid-recovery rides the in-process
backoff-retry (no restart noise): resolves -> forward completion; exhausts -> classified
rollback with the cause named (STATBUS-109/190).
TEST c-rollback-resurrection-arc: a failed fix-release rolls back onto the DISPLACED version's
binary — the superseded row is NEVER resurrected through any door; completed stays
serve-proven (STATBUS-160); the refuse names the re-dispatch remedy.
GAP -> FIX history (surfaced RED by the preswap backup kill, pre-arc era):
ROOT: rollback() restarted the DB then reconnected with NO DB-health-wait — asymmetric with
applyPostSwap's waitForDBHealth(30s) (service.go:3780) — so the reconnect raced the DB
restart and transiently failed. The terminal UPDATE was then single-shot, silently swallowed,
and the flag removed unconditionally -> row stranded in_progress. The retry alone would only
have papered over the missing wait.
FIX (1) add waitForDBHealth(30s) after restart, before reconnect — the root fix, symmetric with
the normal path (drawn above). (2) the terminal write retries the FULL reconnect (re-acquiring
the upgrade_daemon AUTHORITY lock, service.go:2660 / 1922) + markTerminal on exhaustion +
removeUpgradeFlag ONLY on a landed write (KEEP on failure). On lock-contention, YIELD to the
authority — the belt reconciles; never bypass the lock.
